questions.question: What must you NOT do to a moving vehicle ahead of you inside crossing zig-zags?
options: Leave a two-second gap behind it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 bans overtaking any leading moving or stopped vehicle at a crossing.

questions.question: Why do busy crossroads have yellow box junctions?
options: To stop queuing cars from blocking crossing traffic
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 keeps the centre of busy junctions clear for cross traffic.

questions.question: When passing a cyclist riding past parked cars, why leave extra room?
options: A parked car door could suddenly open into the cyclist's path
The cyclist must ride on the kerb
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 notes cyclists ride away from parked cars to avoid opening doors.

questions.question: What is the main danger of driving too close to the car in front?
options: You may not have time to stop if they brake suddenly
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 warns that tailgating leaves no room to stop safely.

questions.question: When should you avoid giving a signal?
options: When it could confuse or mislead other road users
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns not to give misleading signals.

questions.question: Where do street lights usually show a 30 mph limit for cars unless signs say otherwise?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 explains street-lit roads default to 30 mph unless signed.

questions.question: Before joining a busier road from a give-way line, where should you look?
options: Both right and left for vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 tells you to look both ways for all road users before pulling out.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how should your move affect vehicles in the next lane?
options: They should slow down slightly for you
You must not force them to slow down or swerve
You only need to clear cars behind you
You have priority if you signal first
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 states you must not cut in or force others to slow down.

questions.question: When is it safe to enter a roundabout?
options: When there is a safe gap so circulating traffic does not have to slow down
Whenever you reach the line first
Whenever the car in front enters, without looking
Only after stopping for three seconds
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 advises entering only when there is a safe gap to the right.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when taking an exit to the right?
options: No signal until after you leave
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells you to signal right on approach for exits past straight ahead.

questions.question: What signal must you give just before leaving any roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires a left signal as you prepare to leave a roundabout.

questions.question: Which blue sign warns you to keep left of a roundabout island?
options: A blue circle with white arrows pointing clockwise
A red triangle with a cross
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 explains the blue mini-roundabout and roundabout arrows showing clockwise flow.

questions.question: What happens if you drift sideways out of your lane on a roundabout?
options: You could collide with a car or cyclist beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 warns against cutting across another driver's lane when circulating.

questions.question: Which approach lane should you use for an exit past straight ahead (turning right)?
options: The right-hand lane, unless signs say otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 states to use the right-hand lane when taking an exit to the right.

questions.question: What should you do before signalling to pull over and stop?
options: Check your mirrors to see who is behind you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 works with mirror checks so others understand your signal.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car on a dual carriageway with a central barrier?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 70 mph for cars on dual carriageways unless signed lower.

questions.question: What shape is a red-and-white Give Way sign?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 uses the inverted red-and-white triangle for Give Way.

questions.question: What should you do right after checking your mirrors before changing lanes?
options: Check your blind spot over your shoulder
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says to check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What road marking sits across each entrance to a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 marks roundabout entrances with broken give-way lines.

questions.question: How do you signal on approach when taking the first exit to the left?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires a left signal on approach for the first exit.

questions.question: Where does the no-overtaking rule at a zebra crossing apply?
options: Within the zig-zag zone on the approach to the crossing
Only on the black and white stripes
Only after you pass the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 applies across the zig-zag markings approaching the crossing.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but cars are queued just past the box junction. What should you do?
options: Drive into the box so cars behind you can cross
Wait behind the junction until space opens beyond the box
Sound your horn to make the queue move
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 says you must wait before the box even on a green light if the exit is blocked.

questions.question: What should you do if a cyclist is riding in the middle of the lane in slow town traffic?
options: Stay patiently behind them and do not force past
Sound your horn until they move over
Squeeze past inches from their handlebar
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 and H1/H2 respect cyclists' safe road position.

questions.question: What should you do if a car pulls into your safe two-second gap?
options: Sound your horn and stay close
Ease off gently to rebuild your two-second gap
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 advises dropping back smoothly whenever the gap shrinks.

questions.question: When taking the first exit to the left, what happens to your left signal?
options: Keep signalling left all the way around into the exit
Cancel it at the give-way line
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps the left signal on from approach through the first exit.

questions.question: Why must you NEVER drive anti-clockwise around a roundabout?
options: You would drive head-on into oncoming circulating traffic
It wears out the left tyres
It is allowed only for emergency vans
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 prevents head-on collisions by keeping all traffic clockwise.

questions.question: Why do many drivers drift out of lane on roundabouts?
options: Looking only at the kerb instead of planning their path around the curve
Holding the steering wheel with both hands
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 advises looking ahead along your lane path to hold a clean line.

questions.question: Why should you choose your roundabout approach lane early?
options: To avoid last-second swerving across other drivers
So you do not need signals
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 encourages early lane selection for smooth, safe driving.

questions.question: Does the zig-zag no-overtaking rule apply at signal-controlled crossings like pelican crossings too?
options: Yes, it applies at all pedestrian crossings with zig-zags
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 applies to zebra, pelican, puffin, and toucan crossings with zig-zags.

questions.question: What should you do if a car in front stops inside a box junction and leaves no room on the far side?
options: Wait behind the box line until space opens past the box
Drive onto the yellow lines behind them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 requires waiting outside the box until your exit is clear.

questions.question: In wet or windy weather, how should you adjust your overtaking gap past a cyclist?
options: Leave even more space than usual
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 advises extra clearance in poor weather or strong side winds.

questions.question: What happens to your view ahead when you leave a proper two-second gap?
options: You can see past the vehicle ahead and spot hazards earlier
You see less of the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 notes a wider gap improves your view of road hazards.

questions.question: When turning right at a small mini-roundabout, what mistake do learners sometimes make?
options: Cutting the corner on the wrong side of the white circle
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 warn drivers not to cut across the wrong side of the central marking.

questions.question: At a roundabout with three approach lanes, the middle lane is marked straight ahead. Which lane should you use to go straight?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says to follow painted lane markings on multi-lane approaches.

questions.question: If you want to change lanes while circulating on a roundabout, what must you do first?
options: Check mirrors and blind spot, signal, and wait for a clear gap
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 133 require full checks before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you signal early, does that give you the right to pull out?
options: Yes, other drivers must stop for you
No, you must still wait until it is safe
Yes, if you signal for three seconds
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 reminds drivers that signals show intent and never give priority.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car on a single-lane-each-way rural road?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 60 mph for cars on single rural roads without lower signs.

questions.question: What should you do if a car is already on the roundabout to your right and close?
options: Stop behind the give-way line and wait for a safe gap
Accelerate hard in front of it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 requires waiting until there is a safe gap.

questions.question: When should you start your approach signal for a roundabout?
options: In good time before reaching the give-way line
After you are already on the roundabout
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 103 require early, clear approach signals.

questions.question: When turning left from a side road onto a main road, which direction is the main danger first?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 checks right first for nearside flow, and left for overtaking traffic.

questions.question: In slow queuing traffic, when should you change lanes?
options: Whenever a tiny gap opens for a moment
Only when it is safe and you will not block others
As fast as possible before the queue stops
Without signalling so others do not speed up
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 advises not weaving between lanes or cutting across other drivers.

questions.question: After you have entered the exit road from a roundabout, what should you do?
options: Check your left signal has cancelled
Leave the left signal on for 300 metres
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 103 require cancelling your signal once clear.

questions.question: In heavy rain, why do blind-spot checks matter even more before changing lanes?
options: Spray reduces what you can see in side mirrors
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 and wet-weather advice warn that spray hides vehicles in mirrors.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, why can it be hard to give a separate left exit signal?
options: The junction is very small, so keep your focus on steering safely if tight
Left signals are banned at mini-roundabouts
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 188 note there is less time to signal exit at very small mini-roundabouts.

questions.question: May you overtake a parked car that broke down on the zig-zags? Only if safe?
options: Wait if unsure, and pass slowly only if it is clearly stationary and broken down, watching for pedestrians
Never pass a broken-down car even after checking
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids overtaking moving or stopped-for-crossing lead vehicles; pass broken-down obstructions only with extreme care.

questions.question: Which turning direction has the special exception to wait inside a yellow box junction?
options: Turning right (when only oncoming traffic stops you)
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 grants the exception only for right turns blocked by oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Approaching a blind hill crest behind a slow cyclist, what should you do?
options: Wait behind until you can see the oncoming road is clear
Overtake on the blind crest anyway
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 and Rule 166 forbid overtaking where you cannot see far enough ahead.

questions.question: If a driver behind is tailgating you, how should you respond?
options: Ease off slightly to leave more space in front so you can brake gently
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 advises increasing your front gap so neither car has to brake sharply.

questions.question: What should you check before cancelling a signal early if you change your mind?
options: That nobody has already reacted to your first signal
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 stresses clear, unambiguous signals at all times.

questions.question: What happens when variable gantry signs show a speed inside a red ring on a motorway?
options: That lower limit is legally enforced
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 and 258 make red-ring gantry limits legally binding.
